qs.q: What differentiates Huntington’s disease from Parkinson’s disease in terms of its origin?
o: Huntington’s disease is an acute infectious condition
Huntington’s disease lacks any trinucleotide repeats
Huntington’s disease is exclusively caused by viral integration
qs.e: Huntington’s disease is genetically inherited and caused by a mutation in the HTT gene, unlike neurodegenerative conditions caused solely by environmental factors. It is not an infection.
qs.s: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) — Principles, Steps & Clinical: MCQs

qs.q: Which genetic feature within the HTT gene expands beyond normal limits in individuals affected by Huntington’s disease?
qs.e: In Huntington's disease, the CAG trinucleotide repeat expands beyond 36 times, making the gene abnormally large. Normal individuals have fewer than 30 repeats.
qs.s: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) — Principles, Steps & Clinical: MCQs

qs.q: How is the PCR product analyzed after amplifying the HTT gene to confirm a diagnosis of Huntington’s disease?
qs.e: Gel electrophoresis is performed to compare the size of the PCR product with a normal control sample. Sequencing is not the primary sizing method used here.
qs.s: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) — Principles, Steps & Clinical: MCQs

qs.q: What is the primary reason why PCR is valuable in diagnosing genetic disorders like cystic fibrosis and Huntington's disease?
o: It immediately cures the underlying cellular defect in cells
It converts abnormal proteins back into normal folding patterns
It allows early genetic screening and identification of mutations
It permanently replaces the mutated gene sequence in vivo
qs.e: PCR enables early identification of mutations and genetic screening, aiding diagnosis and counseling. It is a diagnostic tool, not a therapeutic gene-editing treatment.
qs.s: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) — Principles, Steps & Clinical: MCQs

qs.q: In Huntington disease, when does conversion from premutation to full mutation occur?
o: Limited to a single tissue compartment
qs.e: Unlike fragile X syndrome where expansion occurs during oogenesis, in Huntington disease and some other trinucleotide repeat disorders, premutations are converted to full mutations during spermatogenesis.
qs.s: SINGLE-GENE DISORDERS WITH ATYPICAL INHERITANCE MCQs

qs.q: Hyperkinetic features in Huntington's disease are due to loss of ---
qs.e: Huntington's disease involves the specific loss of striatal medium spiny neurons that use GABA and acetylcholine.

qs.q: A 40-year-old man develops progressive choreiform movements and dementia. His father had similar symptoms. Which mutation is most likely? Huntington disease (autosomal dominant, CAG repeat expansion). ---
o: Missense mutation in the FBN1 gene
Trinucleotide repeat expansion in HTT gene
Large deletion in the CFTR gene
Deleterious mutation in the TP53 gene
qs.e: Huntington disease is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by a trinucleotide repeat expansion in the HTT gene.
qs.s: Pathology by Dr. Irungu — MCQ Bank

qs.q: In Huntington disease, the conversion from premutation to full mutation primarily occurs during which process?
qs.e: In Huntington disease, the unstable CAG repeat expansion (premutation to full mutation) primarily occurs during spermatogenesis, leading to paternal transmission bias for earlier onset.
